lead_intro: Have you ever thought about living in complete solitude like a hermit? In this 6 Minute English episode, Neil and Rob discuss the reasons why some people choose to live alone. Let's dive into a quiz based on the intriguing story of Christopher Wright, the hermit of the Maine woods!

quiz.question: Why did Christopher Wright, the hermit of the Maine woods, need an alarm clock?
choices: a) to remind him when to hide his tent?
b) to frighten away wild animals?
c) to wake him up at the coldest part of the night so he didn't freeze to death?
quiz.answer: c) to wake him up at the coldest part of the night so he didn't freeze to death?
quiz.explanation: Christopher Wright needed an alarm clock to wake him up at the coldest part of the night so he didn't freeze to death in the Maine woods.

quiz.question: What does Confucius's dictum advise?
choices: a) to always serve the Emperor
b) to become a recluse when the Emperor is good
c) to become a recluse when the Emperor is evil
quiz.answer: c) to become a recluse when the Emperor is evil
quiz.explanation: Confucius's dictum advised that when the Emperor was evil, people should become recluses - living alone and avoiding contact with others.

quiz.question: How does Sara Maitland suggest parents should use 'Go to your room!'?
quiz.explanation: Sara Maitland suggests that parents should use 'Go to your room!' as a reward or treat for children, teaching them that being alone can be enjoyable.

quiz.question: What is the modern way of saying 'to recluse'?
quiz.explanation: The modern way of saying 'to recluse' is 'to drop out' - rejecting the normal ways society works and living outside the system.

quiz.question: Why do many people experience solitude according to Sara Maitland?
quiz.explanation: Sara Maitland mentions that most people experience solitude after a bereavement, such as the death of a relative or close friend.
